decisions.rationale: Leading Scizor and Pelipper sets immediate Drizzle to halve Fire-type damage (Altaria's Flamethrower) while threatening heavy Steel STAB with Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch and Speed control via Tailwind/Wide Guard against Hyper Voice. Archaludon and Basculegion in the back capitalize on Rain with instant Electro Shot and Swift Swim sweeping.

Lead Cloud Nine Altaria + Follow Me Unaware Clefable to blank rain/Swift Swim/Electro Shot and soak Fake Out/SD/Stamina. Back Mega Floette for the Archaludon nuke and sash Dedenne to delete Pelipper; leave the physical attackers for a later game once their mega and rain sequencing are known.

Altaria threatens Scizor with a Cloud Nine-boosted Flamethrower. Protecting with Scizor while evolving allows Scizor to safely Mega Evolve and scout/block incoming attacks, while Pelipper sets Tailwind to secure speed control for the rest of the game.
Cloud Nine stays up if we do not Mega. Flamethrower can KO or cripple Scizor before Pelipper moves; Follow Me beats Bullet Punch and pulls both single-target attacks off Altaria.

Altaria threatens Mega Scizor with a high-damage or OHKO Flamethrower under Cloud Nine. Switching Scizor out to Archaludon cleanly absorbs Flamethrower or Dragon/Fairy/Electric moves while preserving Scizor for the late game against the opponent's Fairy team. Under Tailwind, Pelipper outspeeds Altaria and lands a heavy Hurricane into Altaria.

Keep Cloud Nine so rain stays suppressed and Flamethrower is not halved; Follow Me covers Altaria from Tailwind-fast BP+Hurricane while Flamethrower pressures Mega Scizor (possible OHKO, Wide Guard cannot stop it). Mega now would drop Cloud Nine before the attack and ruin the Fire KO.

Archaludon outspeeds under Tailwind and uses Flash Cannon to easily KO Clefable (guaranteed KO from 53%), redirecting or not. Pelipper targets Altaria with Hurricane to chip it down while Rain remains active.

Keep Cloud Nine up and Protect Altaria so Draco Meteor cannot remove it. Pivot the 53% Clefable into sash Dedenne so a predicted Flash Cannon cannot KO the redirector; both mons live and Dedenne threatens Pelipper next.
Archaludon is faster than Dedenne under Tailwind (210 vs 168 max) and Flash Cannon has 100% accuracy to cleanly finish the 1% Sash Dedenne before it can act. Pelipper targets Altaria with Hurricane.

Dedenne is guaranteed to KO Pelipper with Thunderbolt if it lives; Clefable switch-in plus Follow Me last turn makes Archaludon the only realistic redirect target, and Flash Cannon is a guaranteed KO on 53% Clefable. Switching Altaria to Clefable therefore soaks the Steel move, Dedenne deletes Pelipper, and we keep Cloud Nine Altaria plus Mega Floette for the next turn.

Send Altaria for Cloud Nine to shut off remaining rain (no instant Electro Shot, Hurricane no longer auto-hits, Swift Swim Basculegion neutered) and to threaten Mega Scizor with Flamethrower. Floette is the worse lead into Flash Cannon and into Scizor; keep mega unused so Floette can still Fairy-Aura nuke Archaludon later. Clefable can only pass.
Archaludon's Flash Cannon cleanly KOs Clefable regardless of Follow Me, while Pelipper resets Tailwind to maintain decisive speed control against Altaria and the opponent's final Pokémon.

Confused Clefable is KO'd by Flash Cannon/Electro Shot and likely Hurricane; Follow Me still redirects every single-target hit so healthy Cloud Nine Altaria cannot be Draco'd. Do not Mega (Pixilate drops Cloud Nine while rain still has a turn; Flash Cannon becomes 2x). Spend the free Altaria turn chipping Archaludon with Flamethrower rather than a weak Hyper Voice.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Under Tailwind, Archaludon (210) and Pelipper (170) both outspeed Floette-Eternal (112-144) and Altaria (100-132). Archaludon's Flash Cannon (64.1-114.1%) combined with Pelipper's Hurricane (30.4-53%) guarantees a KO on Floette-Eternal before it can move (even with max bulk, 64.1% + 30.4% minimum rolls + Hurricane 70% accuracy / worst case still leaves it in Bullet Punch range for 100% HP Mega Scizor in the back). Double targeting Floette-Eternal eliminates their main offensive threat.

Floette Protects through Tailwind-boosted Flash Cannon (75-111%, likely KO) while Mega gives Fairy Aura and bulk; non-mega LoR already KOs Arch from 46% so Aura is not required for the KO. Altaria must not Mega (Cloud Nine stays up). Tailwind equalizes speed if she lives; if they Draco her instead Floette is still intact to delete Arch next turn.

Floette-Mega moves faster under Tailwind and threatens a KO on Archaludon with Light of Ruin/Moonblast. Archaludon using Protect guarantees survival and shields against incoming attacks, while Pelipper targets Floette-Mega with Hurricane to chip it down into Bullet Punch range for Mega Scizor next turn.

Moonblast is a 100% acc guaranteed KO on 46% Arch before it moves; LoR is worse (90% + recoil). Arch Protect is the main answer, so Altaria Flamethrowers Pelipper (Wide Guard-proof chip). If Arch stays and faints, the Fire shot can retarget Pelipper; doubling Arch would waste the Fire into Protect.

Archaludon targets Floette-Mega with Flash Cannon to secure the KO if it survives or if Floette attacks Pelipper/misses, while Pelipper also attacks Floette-Mega with Hurricane to ensure damage pressure and cover potential plays.
Switching Scizor in gives immediate priority KO on Floette-Mega next turn with Bullet Punch and Protect against Altaria's Flamethrower.

Floette outspeeds Arch and Moonblast is a 100% KO from 46%, so Arch faints before Flash Cannon if it stays and does not Protect. That keeps Floette alive through Pelipper (Hurricane/Hydro cannot KO 57%). LoR is worse (90% and recoil plus Hurricane KOs). Altaria Flamethrower chips sashless Pelipper; Hyper Voice and Protect add less.

Scizor's priority Bullet Punch KOs the 17% Mega Floette before it can attack. Pelipper sets Tailwind on the turn the opponent's Tailwind expires, guaranteeing that our backline Basculegion and remaining forces outspeed Altaria on Turn 10 even under Cloud Nine.

Floette is KO'd by BP or Hurricane, so Protect keeps her. Altaria Flamethrowers Scizor (4x, possible OHKO) to punish SD/attack; HH-Flame still isn't a guaranteed KO and sacrifices Floette into a losing 1v2.

Mega Scizor's priority Bullet Punch cleanly finishes off Mega Floette before it can act, while Pelipper attacks Altaria with Hurricane to set up a decisive endgame with Basculegion waiting in reserve.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Scizor BP and Pelipper Hurricane/Hydro all KO 18% Floette; Floette is slower so attacks never land unless it lives. Consecutive Protect is 1/3 but strictly dominates attacking. Altaria Flamethrower is a guaranteed Scizor KO if they do not Protect it.
Altaria is the opponent's final Pokémon at 46% HP. Basculegion outspeeds under Tailwind and Last Respects (150 BP after 2 faints) is a guaranteed KO through its Cloud Nine.
Floette is gone so pass; Protect is the only action that lives through guaranteed Last Respects and possible Hurricane KOs. No remaining KO path this game.
Altaria is at 46% HP and cannot Mega Evolve since Floette already Mega Evolved. Basculegion outspeeds under Tailwind and guarantees a KO with Last Respects. Pelipper covers with Hurricane.
Last Respects (BP 150) is a guaranteed KO from 46%; Protect is the only non-zero survival line despite the reduced rate. Attacks cannot KO either foe.

Altaria is at 46% HP after protecting twice in a row, and Floette already used the opponent's Mega Evolution earlier, meaning Altaria remains Dragon/Flying with Cloud Nine and cannot Pixilate Hyper Voice. Basculegion's Last Respects is a guaranteed KO on Altaria, while Pelipper's Wide Guard prevents spread damage if Altaria attempts Hyper Voice.
Last Respects is a guaranteed KO and Protect is the only remaining out; streak odds are poor but attacking or Tailwind cannot win.

reflections.summary: Our Steel-type offensive pressure from Archaludon and Scizor tore through their Fairy core and redirection, while Pelipper's Tailwind ensured Scizor and Basculegion cleaned up the endgame.
reflections.adjustment: Account for non-Mega Cloud Nine Altaria running Flamethrower and Tailwind to prevent surprise heavy damage into Scizor and Archaludon.

reflections.summary: Cloud Nine fairy core traded Archaludon and Mega Scizor but Dedenne never moved and died to Flash Cannon, so Pelipper’s sash stayed up and lone Altaria lost the 1v2 to Life Orb Last Respects after consecutive Protect failed.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Mimikyu for Last Respects immunity; only keep Dedenne if it can actually snipe Pelipper sash—do not send it into Archaludon.

events.text: Floette used Light of Ruin → Archaludon

decisions.rationale: Leading Scizor and Archaludon provides immense double Steel offensive and defensive pressure against the opponent's all-Fairy roster, with Pelipper and Basculegion in the back to clean up under Rain/Tailwind.
Lead Unaware Follow Me + Cloud Nine to cover rain Swift Swim and a possible Fake Out pivot; Floette Mega and Mimikyu in back for Dragon immunity/Fairy Aura pressure and the Last Respects answer.

Altaria threatens Scizor with a potential 4x Flamethrower OHKO, so Scizor uses Protect + Mega Evolve to scout/sculpt tempo safely. Clefable will likely click Follow Me or Thunder Wave. Archaludon's Flash Cannon targets Clefable (and redirected or direct, hits Fairy super-effectively for 74.3-134.1%), preserving Scizor while exerting heavy Steel pressure.

Follow Me blanks Arch Draco (guaranteed Altaria KO) while Cloud Nine stays up so Electro Shot cannot fire and rain stays offline. Flamethrower pressures Scizor now (76–143%) instead of gifting a Mega+SD turn; do not Mega or Tailwind into a possible Pelipper switch.

Clefable is dead so we must send a replacement. Mimikyu is the safer switch-in: Disguise eats one hit from Scizor or Archaludon, Ghost/Fairy resists Flash Cannon and is only neutral to Bullet Punch, and it immediately pressures their Last Respects closer. Floette-Eternal is too frail into this pair and Flower Veil does nothing for Altaria; Mega Floette can wait until rain is off the table. Altaria has no legal action this turn.

Dual Wingbeat breaks Mimikyu's Disguise and deals substantial damage on the second hit, while Archaludon's Draco Meteor threatens a guaranteed OHKO on Altaria if it does not Mega Evolve / Protect, eliminating the primary Fire threat.
Arch Draco OHKOs Altaria and strips Cloud Nine; Protect is the only safe answer. Mimikyu WoWs Scizor after any BP (Disguise holds) to cripple the physical Mega.

Altaria used Protect last turn and cannot reliably Protect again. Archaludon's Draco Meteor guarantees an OHKO on Altaria, while Scizor's Bullet Punch targets Mimikyu-Busted with priority to finish it off or heavily chip it, maintaining full control of the match.
Arch Flash Cannon KOs busted Mimikyu and Draco OHKOs Altaria; Protect the guaranteed KO and switch Floette into the Draco (Fairy immune). Keep Cloud Nine in back—do not Mega.

Bullet Punch onto Mimikyu (which just used Protect turn 3 and is at 68% with Disguise broken) applies strong priority pressure to finish it or put it in range, while Archaludon targets Floette-Eternal with super-effective Flash Cannon.

Mega Floette before moves turns LoR into a guaranteed Arch OHKO on a hit via Fairy Aura+Spa, and Floette outspeeds so Arch never Flash Cannons if it stays. Play Rough the same slot breaks a sash switch-in and adds chip. Keep Altaria unmega'd for Cloud Nine.

Both Mimikyu (3% HP) and Floette-Mega (5% HP) are in range of a single hit. Bullet Punch on Scizor-Mega will KO Mimikyu, while Archaludon's Flash Cannon will KO Floette-Mega. Even if Mimikyu uses Shadow Sneak or Floette attacks, neither can KO our Pokémon.

Both are BP/FC KO range. Competent line is BP Floette to stop Moonblast plus FC the other slot. Switch Mimikyu to Altaria (Cloud Nine vs expected rain) and Protect Floette: Floette is guaranteed to live BP; Altaria lives BP and lives FC (dies only to a Draco-on-switch read). Keeps the Archaludon-KO threat for next turn.
Scizor-Mega uses Bullet Punch into Floette-Mega to secure the KO on the 5% Fairy before it can act. Archaludon targets Altaria with Draco Meteor for a guaranteed KO from 63% HP.
Protect Altaria through Draco; Moonblast is a 100% KO on Arch if they do not priority-snipe Floette. Keep Cloud Nine up and never Mega Altaria.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Mimikyu is at 3% HP and faints to Scizor's priority Bullet Punch. Altaria used Protect on turn 6 (protect counter reduced) and is at 63% HP, which is a guaranteed KO from Archaludon's Draco Meteor. Even if Mimikyu uses Shadow Sneak first, it deals minimal damage to Scizor.
Send in Basculegion to finish the 3% HP Mimikyu next turn with Aqua Jet alongside Archaludon.

Mimikyu is dead to any hit so Protect it. Altaria must Flamethrower Scizor now: it is a possible KO from 71% and the only way to punish a Protect/SD/BP-Mimikyu turn. Consecutive Protect on Altaria is only 1/3 and Draco Meteor is a guaranteed KO if it fails. Hyper Voice does nothing useful.

Mimikyu is at 3% HP with broken Disguise and just used Protect on Turn 7. Aqua Jet from Basculegion covers any non-priority move and finishes Mimikyu even through Speed advantage, while Archaludon Flash Cannon backs it up.
Mimikyu dies to Aqua Jet/LR/Flash Cannon from 4%. Shadow Sneak outspeeds Aqua Jet and chips Basculegion before the KO; Protect is only 1/3 and delays the same loss.

reflections.summary: Won Game 2 and the series 2-0 by exploiting the opponent's extreme Fairy weakness with a double-Steel lead of Mega Scizor and Archaludon. Turn 1 Scizor Protect absorbed Altaria's Flamethrower while Archaludon's Flash Cannon deleted Clefable through Follow Me. Even after Scizor was burned, Dual Wingbeat popped Mimikyu's Disguise, and continuous Flash Cannon/Bullet Punch offensive pressure eliminated Mega Floette and Altaria before Basculegion sealed the sweep.
reflections.adjustment: Against this Fairy-heavy roster, the Mega Scizor + Archaludon lead with Basculegion and Pelipper in reserve is optimal; in a future series, maintain this gameplan while keeping Archaludon targeting with Flash Cannon rather than locking into Draco Meteor on predicted Fairy switches.

reflections.summary: Lost game 2 and the series 0-2. Piloting had zero decision errors; the loss was matchup plus variance, not misclicks. G1 notes correctly identified Cloud Nine Altaria (never Mega), Mega Floette, and Mimikyu as the plan, and that package did useful work (burn on Scizor, Draco immunity, disguise, Flamethrower KO on Mega Scizor) but did not flip the series. Preview was the bigger miss: Clefable+Altaria into Scizor+Arch invited turn-1 Protect + Flash Cannon through Follow Me and an instant KO, after which a Light of Ruin miss and a crit Bullet Punch left Mimikyu on fumes for Life Orb Aqua Jet. Registered six are almost all Fairy and are structurally soft to this Steel+Basculegion core; Azumarill (and the unused Water/Fairy Primarina left out of the six) was the material alternative and stayed on the bench.
reflections.adjustment: Register at least one Steel-resistant Water/Fairy (Azumarill or Primarina) and lead it, not Clefable, into Scizor+Arch. Keep Cloud Nine Altaria unmegaed and Mega Floette; do not Follow Me a Flash Cannon. Prep Last Respects/Aqua Jet Basculegion as the actual closer even when rain is broken.

decisions.rationale: Lead Weavile and Sinistcha to combine Fake Out with Imprison against the opposing Trick Room core, while Sableye and Rotom-Wash provide priority disruption and broad answers in the back.

Lead Hatterene + Farigiraf to combine Magic Bounce (reflect status) and Armor Tail (block Fake Out/Prankster priority), neutralizing Weavile/Toxicroak/Sableye disruption and reflecting status. Back Armarouge (Fire for Toxicroak/DrySkin) and Crabominable (Ice/Fighting for Sinistcha/Kommo-o, slow Mega synergy with Trick Room). Exclude Rhyperior (Earthquake/Rock Slide spread hits ally) and Slowbro (redundant special wall, low SpD when Mega).
Fake Out Hatterene prevents its immediate Trick Room attempt, while Sinistcha's Imprison blocks Trick Room from both opposing Pokémon for the rest of the field state.

Double Trick Room is the only way to guarantee setting Trick Room turn 1 against Weavile's turn-1-only Fake Out, which can flinch at most one of our setters. Trick Room is our win condition: it succeeds against every Sinistcha action except Imprison (RagePowder/MatchaGotcha/Trick Room all leave our field TR intact, and RagePowder does not redirect a field move). The lone failure case (Imprison) is recoverable on turn 2 by switching in Crabominable for super-effective Ice damage on Sinistcha to break the Imprison. Single TR + Protect loses to Weavile simply flinching the unprotected setter, so double TR strictly maximizes our TR odds.

Knock Off targets Farigiraf for a possible OHKO while removing its Sitrus Berry; Matcha Gotcha adds spread damage and can finish Farigiraf if Knock Off rolls low, while Imprison continues blocking Trick Room.

Sinistcha's Imprison is the only thing blocking our Trick Room win condition, so concentrating fire on Sinistcha is the priority. Dazzling Gleam (spread, also breaks Weavile's sash) + Farigiraf Psychic on Sinistcha combine for ~68–130% (Sitrus-dependent) — a real KO chance. This line is robust to a likely Rage Powder redirect (both hits then concentrate on Sinistcha instead of wasting Hyper Voice, which is immune to Ghost), and our attacks are not status moves so Weavile's Taunt cannot stop them. Weavile's Focus Sash means it can't be KO'd this turn anyway, so pressuring Sinistcha advances our plan.
Knock Off guarantees the KO on Farigiraf if it does not Protect, while Matcha Gotcha adds a second chance to finish it and pressures Hatterene through spread damage.
Switch Weavile to Rotom-Wash to preserve a durable answer to the opponent’s remaining Water-, Ground-, and Fire-oriented possibilities while minimizing incoming spread damage; Sinistcha must pass.

Dazzling Gleam guarantees Weavile's KO (4% HP, Focus Sash inert off-full) and chips Sinistcha 29-56% (not a guaranteed KO at 31%). Farigiraf cannot damage Sinistcha (Hyper Voice/Psychic both immune) and at 5% HP is a dead weight, so switching it to Armarouge brings in Fire Blast which guarantees Sinistcha's KO next turn (67-128%). Armarouge at 100% HP easily survives the foes' parting Icy Wind/Matcha Gotcha, yielding a far stronger Hatterene+Armarouge board versus the opponent's two unrevealed Pokémon.

Hatterene can only Pass (Forfeit concedes). Bring healthy Crabominable (100% HP) rather than fragile Farigiraf (5% HP): Crabominable's bulk survives Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha and its Ice Hammer KOs the 7% Sinistcha or forces a switch that ends Imprison, freeing Trick Room for our slow attackers while preserving our strongest remaining Pokémon.

Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Hatterene before it can move. Switching Sinistcha to Sableye preserves the 7% HP Imprison user and avoids a possible Crabominable Ice Hammer KO, while keeping strong priority disruption for the next turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Hatterene at 19% brn is guaranteed KO'd by Rotom Hydro Pump (51.5-76.9%) or Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha (29.1-42.5%), so it must Protect to survive and keep our Fairy/Trick Room piece alive one more turn. Crabominable Ice Hammer is 88.8-161.6% into the 7% Sinistcha — a guaranteed KO that removes Imprison (unblocking Trick Room) and a threat. Mega Evolving now commits our only healthy win condition, gaining a large Attack/Defense boost for the impending 1v2 vs Rotom + the hidden mon, with negligible speed cost since everything already out-speeds us; the boosted Ice Hammer still KOs Sinistcha.
Hydro Pump reliably KOs Hatterene before it can act. Matcha Gotcha damages Crabominable-Mega and restores Sinistcha, preserving a chance if Crabominable misses or targets Rotom.

Sinistcha at 7% is the priority KO. Crabominable-Mega Ice Hammer (2x SE) guarantees the KO; Hatterene's Dazzling Gleam is a spread move that also KOs Sinistcha if Ice Hammer's 90% accuracy roll misses, is immune to Sinistcha's potential RagePowder redirection, and chips Rotom-Wash (27-53%). This removes Sinistcha this turn, leaving only Rotom-Wash, which Crabominable finishes next turn with Close Combat (63-116%, possible OHKO). Trick Room is blocked by Sinistcha's Imprison, and Protect wastes Hatterene's remaining offensive value.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Electroweb reliably finishes Farigiraf while lowering Mega Crabominable's Speed; Matcha Gotcha applies spread pressure before likely being targeted, and Imprison already prevents the foes' Trick Room.

Crabominable Ice Hammer KOs low-HP Sinistcha (2x Ice, 23% HP). Farigiraf Psychic softens Rotom-Wash (100%) so Crabominable can finish it next turn with Close Combat. Farigiraf at 5% dies regardless, so attacking Rotom maximizes damage before going down.
Hydro Pump targets the 35% HP Mega Crabominable and has a chance to KO immediately before it can move; Will-O-Wisp is less decisive and can be blocked by Protect.

Farigiraf is fainted, so slot 1 must Pass. This is a 1v1: opponent's only remaining Pokémon is Rotom-Wash (100% HP). Close Combat is my only move with OHKO potential (63–116% range, possible OHKO), while Ice Hammer (0.5x) and Drain Punch cannot KO. Attacking is my only path to victory; Protecting leads to a stalemate where Rotom-Wash can always burn/Protect to deny my offense and I make no progress. Targeting foe 1 (Rotom-Wash), since foe 2 (Sinistcha) is fainted.

reflections.summary: Won by denying the opponent’s Trick Room plan with Sinistcha’s Imprison, then using Weavile’s Knock Off and Rotom-Wash’s Hydro Pump to remove their Psychic core and Mega Crabominable. The four brought—Weavile, Sinistcha, Rotom-Wash, and Sableye—were broadly well suited; Weavile/Sinistcha were especially effective, while Sableye was the weakest fit into Armor Tail. We had no Mega Stone holder to evolve, and Rotom’s role was sufficient without one.
reflections.adjustment: Against Farigiraf, do not spend priority on Fake Out because Armor Tail blocks it; use direct attacks or non-priority options instead. If the preview is unchanged, preserve the Weavile/Sinistcha anti-Trick-Room lead and use Sableye’s Foul Play or Quash rather than relying on Fake Out.

reflections.summary: Lost because opponent's Sinistcha lead used Imprison on turn 1 to block both Hatterene and Farigiraf from using Trick Room, neutralizing our core strategy. Weavile then knocked out the Armarouge switch-in with super-effective Knock Off, and Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha (with healing) wore down our remaining Pokémon while Rotom-Wash cleaned up with Hydro Pump.
reflections.adjustment: Do not lead with both Trick Room setters against a known Imprison user; instead lead Mega Crabominable alongside Hatterene (or use Protect to stall Imprison) so one TR setter survives for later, and avoid switching Dark-weak Armarouge into Weavile's Knock Off.

decisions.rationale: Lead Weavile and Sinistcha to pressure Trick Room immediately with Knock Off and Imprison while retaining strong speed control. Rotom-Wash handles Mega Crabominable and Rhyperior, while Kommo-o provides broad special damage and a reliable Protect option in the back.

Execute the notebook plan: lead Crabominable-Mega to apply pressure. Partner it with Rhyperior so Rock Slide (spread) breaks Weavile through Sinistcha's Rage Powder redirection and Focus Sash, while Crabominable's Ice Hammer hits Sinistcha for 2x. This avoids a double TR-setter lead vs Imprison. Back Slowbro (Fighting resist + Scald 2x vs Rotom-Wash) and Hatterene (Magic Bounce vs status, Dazzling Gleam 2x vs Sableye/Dark). Armarouge stays benched per the never-switch-into-Weavile rule.
Fake Out prevents Crabominable's immediate Close Combat or Ice Hammer while Sinistcha uses Imprison to shut down the opponent's Trick Room plan.

Crabominable Close Combat (4x into Weavile) plus Rhyperior Rock Slide (2x into Weavile, neutral into Sinistcha) maximize pressure on the faster Fake Out user. If Weavile does not Fake Out, the combined 4x+2x breaks FocusSash for a KO; if it Fake Outs one of our mons, the other still drops Weavile to 1 HP. Rock Slide also chips Sinistcha to help remove Imprison later. No Mega this turn since Mega Crabominable lowers Attack.

Switch Weavile to Rotom-Wash to preserve the nearly fainted slot and bring immediate pressure to Crabominable. Sinistcha uses Matcha Gotcha, which threatens a potential OHKO on Rhyperior while retaining the anti-Trick Room piece.

Ice Hammer on Sinistcha is a guaranteed KO (88.8% min > 74% current), removing the dangerous support that threatens Rhyperior with Matcha Gotcha (up to 125.7%, possible OHKO). Rhyperior Protects to fully negate Matcha Gotcha and Icy Wind, surviving safely. Weavile at 1% is neutralized (finished or forced to switch next turn). This kills Sinistcha while keeping both my Pokémon, leaving me up two usable Pokémon with zero downside risk — strictly better than the aggressive Rock Slide line that risks losing Rhyperior for only a marginal gain.
Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Crabominable before it can act, while Matcha Gotcha pressures Rhyperior for substantial super-effective spread damage and may also KO it.

Rhyperior is the 4x Hydro Pump target and its Protect has reduced success (risky KO), so switch to bulky Slowbro to deny the KO. Crabominable is at 37% and would die to Sinistcha's spread Matcha Gotcha (2x) plus burn, so Protect preserves it. This keeps both mons alive (Slowbro fresh, Crabominable ~63% after burn) for a stronger next turn with a potential Slowbro Mega.
Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Crabominable unless it protects, while Matcha Gotcha pressures both foes and can finish Crabominable through a high roll or chip Slowbro if it protects.

Crabominable is a guaranteed KO target for Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump (31% HP, burn), so we extract value by hitting the key support Sinistcha with Ice Hammer (2x, 44-80%). Slowbro pressures the cleaner Rotom-Wash with Psychic (1x, 24.8-46.4%); if Sinistcha uses RagePowder, the attack redirects to Sinistcha anyway, maintaining focus-fire. No Mega: Crabominable-Mega weakens Ice Hammer (Iron Fist 1.2x on 157 Atk = 188 < 202), and Slowbro-Mega drops SpD to 80 against these special attackers.

Slowbro is forced to pass at 16% and will likely fall next turn; switch in Rhyperior for offensive pressure (Ice Punch 2x into Rotom-Wash, Rock Slide on both) since Hatterene's Trick Room is blocked by Sinistcha's Imprison and Rhyperior offers stronger board impact.
Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Rhyperior, while Matcha Gotcha guarantees the KO on Slowbro and pressures Rhyperior. The two attacks also cover either foe's Protect.

Rhyperior is a guaranteed OHKO from Rotom's Hydro Pump (4x) and Slowbro at 16% is a guaranteed KO from any spread special (Matcha Gotcha/Electroweb). The only safe pivot is Hatterene, which resists both Hydro Pump and Matcha Gotcha at 1x and carries Focus Sash + Magic Bounce — it survives every combination (worst case Hydro Pump + Matcha Gotcha leaves it at 1 HP via Sash). So Rhyperior Protects (forcing Rotom to waste Hydro Pump on the Protect or hit Hatterene at 1x) while the doomed Slowbro switches into Hatterene. This preserves all three of my mons and sets up a stall-chip: Rhyperior Protects while Hatterene's DazzlingGleam grinds Rotom/Sinistcha down, freeing Rhyperior to attack once the Hydro Pump threat is gone. Trick Room is blocked by Sinistcha's Imprison, so it's off the table until Sinistcha leaves.
Rotom-Wash moves first and Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Rhyperior, while Sinistcha's spread Matcha Gotcha pressures Hatterene and preserves the active Imprison lock.

Rhyperior is 4x weak to Rotom's Hydro Pump (guaranteed OHKO) and Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha (4x). Protect has reduced success (~50%) after consecutive uses, an unacceptable coin-flip in a do-or-die game. Switching Rhyperior to Slowbro guarantees it escapes Hydro Pump range — the single-target move fails on the switched-out Pokémon — keeping our strongest attacker healthy on the bench. Slowbro survives the 2x Matcha Gotcha at low HP. Hatterene is our safe anchor (Focus Sash + Magic Bounce, resists both opposing attacks at 1x), so it stays in and uses Dazzling Gleam to chip both Rotom and Sinistcha, making progress against the core. Trick Room is still blocked by Sinistcha's Imprison, so it's unusable.
Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Hatterene, while Matcha Gotcha guarantees the KO on Slowbro, creating the best chance to remove both active foes this turn.

Double-target Sinistcha: Hatterene Dazzling Gleam (spread, 29.2–56.2%) + Slowbro Psychic (27–50%) = min 56.2% > Sinistcha's 56% HP, a guaranteed KO if it doesn't Protect. Sinistcha is the linchpin (Imprison blocks my Trick Room; Matcha Gotcha is 4x into Rhyperior, 2x into Slowbro), so removing it is worth trading Slowbro (already doomed to any spread special). Hatterene's Focus Sash ensures it survives Rotom's Hydro Pump (51.5–76.9% would KO but Sash holds at 1 HP). This opens Trick Room and frees Rhyperior, yielding a cleaner board than stalling into a 2-vs-3 with Sinistcha still enabling the opponent.

Only Rhyperior remains (benched at 100%) versus Sinistcha (80%) + Rotom-Wash (59%) active plus an unrevealed 4th and a 1% Weavile. Rhyperior is 4x weak to both Hydro Pump and Matcha Gotcha, which are spread moves, so it dies the moment it acts while both foes are active and can only stall via Protect. The game is effectively lost, but forfeiting (slot 1 option 2) guarantees a 0-2 series loss, whereas sending Rhyperior in preserves a nonzero chance (opponent misplay/switch, Protect streaks) of extending to game 3. Send Rhyperior into slot 1 and Pass slot 2 since only one Pokémon is left to field.
Double-target Rhyperior with Rotom-Wash’s super-effective Hydro Pump and Sinistcha’s super-effective Matcha Gotcha to secure the knockout before it can act.

Both foes outspeed Rhyperior (106-138 / 90-122 vs 60) and each have a 4x super-effective guaranteed OHKO (Hydro Pump 80% / Matcha Gotcha 90%). Attacking means Rhyperior faints before acting (~98% combined KO chance). Protect (priority +4) is the only move that blocks both and keeps me alive; with the series on the line, survival is the only path to any remaining win chance. Hatterene is fainted so Pass.

Double-target Rhyperior with Hydro Pump and Matcha Gotcha: Hydro Pump guarantees the KO if it connects, while Matcha Gotcha may also KO independently; both have strong accuracy and Rhyperior's consecutive Protect penalty makes attacking optimal.

Only Rhyperior remains against Sinistcha (80%) + Rotom-Wash (65%) + an unrevealed 4th; both Rotom Hydro Pump and Sinistcha Matcha Gotcha are 4x guaranteed OHKOs on Rhyperior, so my only path to stay alive is Protect. Protect maximizes turns survived (best infinitesimal win probability) versus attacking, which dies to Matcha Gotcha/Hydro Pump. Hatterene is fainted, so slot 2 is forced Pass.

reflections.summary: Won 2-0 because the team-preview plan correctly prioritized the Sinistcha–Weavile lead and Rotom-Wash as the main answer to the opponent's Trick Room and physical threats. Sinistcha's Imprison constrained Hatterene's Trick Room plan, while Rotom-Wash steadily removed Crabominable, pressured Slowbro, and finished Rhyperior; Weavile's Focus Sash also preserved its utility after the opening Rock Slide. The four brought—Weavile, Sinistcha, Rotom-Wash, and Kommo-o—suited the matchup, and no Mega Stone holder was evolved. Piloting was clean with no decision errors, although Hydro Pump misses and repeated Rhyperior Protects made the finish less efficient. The between-game adjustment to maintain the anti-Trick Room core and bring Rotom-Wash helped rather than backfired. The registered six were generally sound for this opponent; Sableye was the most replaceable member, but the left-behind options offered no clearly superior alternative based on the revealed composition.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same general four and make Sinistcha's Imprison lead priority against Hatterene-based Trick Room. Preserve Rotom-Wash for Rhyperior and other physical threats, but avoid making the endgame depend entirely on repeated Hydro Pump attempts into Protect; use safer positioning or alternate pressure when available. Treat Hatterene's Magic Bounce and Focus Sash as reasons not to rely on priority disruption or a single status/control interaction. Consider Sableye only if scouting suggests more value from its direct utility than Kommo-o; there is no demonstrated need for a major roster change.

reflections.summary: Lost game 2 and the series 0-2 because the four brought (Crabominable, Rhyperior, Slowbro, Hatterene, with no Mega evolution) were hard-countered by the opponent's Sinistcha+Rotom-Wash core. Rhyperior's 4x weaknesses to Matcha Gotcha (Grass) and Hydro Pump (Water) made it a free target; Sinistcha's Imprison blocked Trick Room and its spread move healed it while burning our mons; Rotom's Levitate nullified our Ground attacks. Between-game adjustments (selecting this team without evolving Mega stones) backfired, repeating the error of exposing Rhyperior and failing to remove Sinistcha. Piloting had 0 decision errors but the team-preview plan was fundamentally mismatched.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series vs this opponent, replace Rhyperior in the brought four with Farigiraf or Armarouge from the registered six to eliminate the 4x weakness to the core's STABs. Evolve Mega Slowbro (or Mega Crabominable) for added bulk/power instead of leaving mega stones unused. Prioritize knocking out Sinistcha before it can Imprison/heal; use Hatterene as safe pivot but avoid repeated Protect (can fail). Attempt Trick Room only after Sinistcha is removed. Never switch Armarouge into Weavile.

decisions.rationale: Lead the double-Drought sun core (Torkoal Eruption + Ninetales Heat Wave/Helping Hand/Encore); back line brings Politoed+Vanilluxe for stacked Icy Wind speed control vs fast Excadrill/Tinkaton, Aurora Veil, a second Helping Hand, and Water Absorb vs Goodra's Muddy Water. Gyarados sits (STABs resisted by their all-Steel roster, 4x Thunderbolt-weak) along with slow Hippowdon.

Lead Aegislash (Wide Guard) + Excadrill to blank their weather spread cores (Eruption/Heat Wave/Blizzard/Icy Wind are all allAdjacentFoes) while Excadrill's Ground/Rock pressure deletes Torkoal/Ninetales/Vanilluxe. Back Mawile (Intimidate + Huge Power vs Mega Gyarados) and Skarmory (Hippowdon wall, Tailwind, Taunt vs Aurora Veil/Yawn/Encore).

Full-HP sun Charcoal Eruption is a guaranteed OHKO on BOTH leads across their legal stat ranges (Excadrill 133-253%, even Shield Aegislash 105-187%), so if Wide Guard is not up this turn alone flips the game. Their obvious counter is Aegislash Wide Guard, so Helping Hand/Heat Wave add nothing (blocked or redundant) while exposing Ninetales to High Horsepower, which is a guaranteed OHKO on her (114-164%). Protect keeps her perfectly safe; Torkoal survives any single hit (worst case 59-83% from HHP). If they do Wide Guard, we lose one turn of sun but head to the Encore punishment line next turn with both leads intact.

Aegislash uses Wide Guard to blank Torkoal's Eruption and Ninetales' Heat Wave (Eruption would OHKO Excadrill). Excadrill Mega Evolves: Mega form's higher Attack (217) guarantees the OHKO on Ninetales with High Horsepower, its Speed 170 outspeeds Ninetales, and its higher Defense (120) lets it survive a Body Press + Helping Hand counterplay that would otherwise KO it. Removing the faster Encore/Helping Hand threat while keeping Wide Guard up is the strongest tempo play.

Full-HP sun Eruption verifiably OHKOs both actives (132.7-253% on Excadrill-Mega, 105.4-186.7% on Aegislash), so Helping Hand is redundant damage. Their only answers are a decaying second Wide Guard (1/3 success) or redirecting High Horsepower onto Torkoal. Encore forces Aegislash to burn its Wide Guard attempt this turn (fails 2/3) and strips WG from their toolkit afterward, so even the blocked branch leaves us free to fire again next turn with Torkoal still at 100%; if Excadrill targets Ninetales again instead, we cash a double KO into a 3v2 with sun up.

Torkoal can only pass this decision. Vanilluxe would face a guaranteed Iron Head OHKO (100-137%) and likely moves after Excadrill, while Politoed resists Iron Head (17-24%), tanks HHP with Sitrus, and its Icy Wind drops every Excadrill roll (90-113) below Vanilluxe's 135 for a safe Veil pivot next turn; Body Press (31-55%, unblockable by Wide Guard) is our damage line on Excadrill.

Torkoal's sun-boosted Eruption OHKOs Excadrill-Mega (166-254%), so Wide Guard is mandatory to keep my board alive. Excadrill outspeeds Ninetales and High Horsepower guarantees the KO on the 60% Ninetales, removing the faster Fire threat while Wide Guard blanks both Eruption and Heat Wave this turn.

Wide Guard has blocked Eruption twice, so firing it again into the pattern is the trap play. Instead execute Plan B's control line: WoW the Excadrill (single-target, WG-proof, 85%) to halve High Horsepower so Torkoal can never be OHKO'd and Vanilluxe entries become safe later, while Politoed Encores Aegislash (also WG-proof) to lock it into Wide Guard for ~3 turns or force a switch - and any replacement that switches in lacks Wide Guard, opening the full-power Eruption lane next turn. Either branch leaves us with burned Excadrill chip via Body Press/Helping Hand and the sun intact.

Torkoal's sun-boosted Charcoal Eruption is a guaranteed OHKO on Excadrill-Mega (166.8-254.5%) and a possible OHKO on Aegislash, so Wide Guard is mandatory to blank both Eruption and Politoed's Icy Wind. With Wide Guard up, Excadrill (170 Spe, fastest) presses High Horsepower into Torkoal: 68.9-120%, a possible OHKO that at minimum cripples Eruption's HP-scaled power for next turn. Sacred Sword chip (16-28%) is not worth dropping Wide Guard, and Rock Slide cannot KO Torkoal.

Aegislash is Encored into Wide Guard, so every spread move (Eruption, Icy Wind) is blocked again this turn, and WG has proven infinitely repeatable. Torkoal at 12% dies to ANY Excadrill click before it moves (it's slower), so staying contributes nothing; its only lasting value is Body Press/WoW, which ignore its HP. Switching banks my sole single-target damage source against the WG wall; worst-case reads (Iron Head/Rock Slide) cost Vanilluxe, but a dead Torkoal loses to WG-stall outright. Politoed's Icy Wind is WG-blocked and Helping Hand whiffs on a switched-out ally, so Encore locks Excadrill into High Horsepower for ~3 turns, denying the Iron Head/Rock Slide that OHKO Vanilluxe while it pivots in and sets Light Clay Aurora Veil.

Excadrill-Mega outspeeds Torkoal and High Horsepower is a guaranteed KO from 12% HP (68.9-120% range). Aegislash is Encored into Wide Guard, which blocks Politoed's Icy Wind (and any Eruption) this turn, keeping Excadrill's Speed intact and board control secure. Switching Aegislash would forfeit that protection for no gain.

Aegislash is Encore-locked into Wide Guard this turn, so every spread move (Icy Wind/Blizzard) is guaranteed blocked and Helping Hand has nothing to boost; Excadrill's Piercing Drill pierces Protect, so Protect saves nobody. Vanilluxe (26%) dies to any HHP regardless of its action, so it sets Aurora Veil for value if Excadrill instead targets Politoed. Politoed takes a null action (Protect) — switching Torkoal in risks feeding our only Body Press/WoW source to a lethal HHP, which doctrine forbids.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Excadrill-Mega's High Horsepower is a guaranteed KO on Vanilluxe from 25% (47.8-90.4% of max), and Piercing Drill even chips through Protect at 1/4 damage, so Vanilluxe dies now or next turn regardless. Aegislash stays locked into Wide Guard, which blanks both foes' Icy Wind/Blizzard spread damage this turn. Excadrill outspeeds everything on their side. This keeps momentum: after Vanilluxe falls, Torkoal at 12% is also deleted by the locked High Horsepower, and Politoed's Water Absorb makes it a non-target we can pivot around later.

No wincon remains: 2v4, Politoed's only attack (Icy Wind) is resisted by every remaining foe and WG-blocked this turn, and both foes are Encore-locked (Exca forced HHP, Aegislash forced WG). Piercing Drill ignores Protect, so 12% Torkoal dies to Excadrill's guaranteed-first HHP regardless. Max-impact line before the loss: Helping Hand + Body Press chips their most dangerous mon 47-81% (WoW's 85% burn is worth less than double the chip here).

Excadrill-Mega's High Horsepower guarantees KO on Torkoal (12% HP; 68.9-120% range), and it outspeeds Torkoal (170 vs 36-64). Aegislash is Encore-locked into Wide Guard, which blocks Politoed's Icy Wind and any Torkoal Eruption, keeping both of my Pokémon safe. Targeting Politoed instead would leave Torkoal alive to Body Press or Will-O-Wisp, so removing the Fire setter now is the clean, safe play.

Game 1 is deterministically lost: Torkoal is fainted and Politoed is my last Pokémon, but its only damaging move (Icy Wind) is a spread move that Aegislash's repeatable Wide Guard blocks and Steel resists, and Encore can't re-lock the already-Encored Excadrill. Excadrill's High Horsepower KOs Politoed within ~3 hits no matter what I choose. Conceding the unwinnable game saves time and moves straight to game 2, where the planned Wide-Guard-proof single-target core (Mega Gyarados + Hippowdon) has a real wincon.

reflections.summary: Lost at team preview, not in execution: all four brought Pokémon dealt damage exclusively through spread moves (Eruption, Heat Wave, Blizzard, Icy Wind), and Aegislash answered with Wide Guard every single turn, erasing 100% of my offense; Body Press is void into Ghost Aegislash and Will-O-Wisp missed, so I inflicted zero damage all game. Mega Excadrill, whose Piercing Drill ignored Ninetales' Protect on turn 1, then knocked out Ninetales, Vanilluxe and Torkoal with repeated super-effective High Horsepower. Piloting was clean: the Encore locks onto Aegislash and Excadrill were the right disruptive calls, and forfeiting a 1v2 with no remaining damage path was correct.
reflections.adjustment: Rebuild the game-2 four around single-target damage from turn 1: Mega Gyarados (Water/Flying is immune to High Horsepower, sets up Dragon Dance freely behind Wide Guard, Crunch hits Aegislash super effectively), Hippowdon (single-target High Horsepower punishes Excadrill, Yawn forces trades), Torkoal for Will-O-Wisp/Body Press support, plus a fourth pick with genuine single-target output. Assume Aegislash uses Wide Guard every turn and Excadrill repeats High Horsepower, and respect Tinkaton Fake Out/Focus Sash and Skarmory Tailwind among the two hidden picks.

reflections.summary: Won by completely neutralizing the opponent's weather-based special offense with Aegislash's Wide Guard, which blocked Torkoal's Eruption and Ninetales' Heat Wave, while Excadrill's High Horsepower tore through their frazzled Fire- and Ice-types. Politoed was the last remaining but couldn't break through.
reflections.adjustment: Be more mindful of Politoed's Encore, which locked Excadrill into High Horsepower; consider bringing a way to reset or play around it, and prepare for the possibility of Gyarados or Hippowdon next game by having a plan for physical attackers and weather control.

decisions.rationale: Bring the planned Gyarados+Hippowdon core (Intimidate, bulky, single-target SE pressure into the all-Steel roster, immune to Wide Guard stall) with Torkoal+Ninetales in back for sun Eruption/Heat Wave once Aegislash is Encored or gone.

Bring Aegislash (Wide Guard blocks their entire spread arsenal: Eruption, Heat Wave, Blizzard, Icy Wind) + Tinkaton (Fake Out flinch, Knock Off strips Charcoal/Heat Rock/Light Clay/Gyaradosite, Stone Edge 2x on Torkoal/Ninetales/Vanilluxe/Gyarados, Focus Sash) as leads to answer both sun and physical leads. Back with Skarmory (walls Gyarados/Hippowdon, immune to High Horsepower, Tailwind/Taunt) and Goodra-Hisui (resists Fire, Thunderbolt 4x Gyarados, Ice Beam 2x Hippowdon, Muddy Water 2x Torkoal/Ninetales). This covers their weather toolbox and the expected Gyarados/Hippowdon counter.

Mega Evolution resolves before moves, so Gyaradosite is locked in before any Knock Off can strip it; Protect (+4 priority) beats Tinkaton's expected Fake Out (+3), burns their once-per-entry Fake Out, and keeps Gyarados clean. Hippowdon's High Horsepower (62.5-117.5%, Focus Sash leaves Tinkaton at 1 HP) pops the Sash and neuters their lead disruptor. All offense is single-target, so the expected Wide Guard spam doesn't block anything.

Tinkaton Fake Out flinches Gyarados to deny its Dragon Dance setup (Tinkaton outspeeds it), while Aegislash uses King's Shield to protect itself from Hippowdon's super-effective Ground/Dark attacks. Tinkaton survives any Hippowdon hit via Focus Sash. This is a safe, tempo-preserving opening against the biggest threat.

Aegislash's King's Shield is only 1/3 to succeed after its successful T1 use, so Crunch (54-95% into Shield forme, and Gyarados always outspeeds Aegislash) is safe major value; worst-case Tinkaton Play Rough (-1, 30-48%) plus Sacred Sword (-1, 30-37%) still leaves Gyarados alive at >=15%. Hippowdon's Crunch (100% accurate vs HHP's 95%) guarantees the 1% Tinkaton dies, removing the permanent 2x Play Rough threat to my Mega.

Tinkaton is at 1% and dies to anything, so maximize its value with Play Rough on Gyarados-Mega (30-53% chip). Aegislash attacking would drop to frail Blade Forme and likely die to Hippowdon; instead switch to Skarmory, who is immune to Hippowdon's Ground moves, has Sturdy+Sitrus, and whose super-effective Body Press (40-69%) can finish the chipped Gyarados next turn while Aegislash is preserved for later.

Keep Skarmory in (no forfeit) and bring Goodra-Hisui over Aegislash. Goodra threatens Gyarados-Mega with Thunderbolt and Hippowdon with Ice Beam (possible KO), resists Water, and is far more durable than Aegislash against the current physical board — Aegislash is 2x weak to both Gyarados Crunch and Hippowdon High Horsepower, and would be forced into frail Blade Forme to threaten anything. Preserve Aegislash's Wide Guard on the bench for the weather back line (Eruption/Heat Wave/Blizzard).

Switching Gyarados out for Torkoal brings Drought sun immediately, and sun Eruption guarantees Skarmory's removal next turn (160-317%, ignores its dormant Sturdy/Sitrus stall) while spreading 44.9-75.5% onto Goodra-Hisui; Hippowdon's High Horsepower chunks Goodra 54.5-98.1% now. This preserves the 60% Gyarados from Thunderbolt (42.5-61.8%, lethal range) and Body Press doubling, keeps Ninetales' Encore in reserve for Aegislash's Wide Guard/King's Shield, and Gyara remains the back-line cleaner.

Set Tailwind with Skarmory to resolve the uncertain Goodra-vs-Hippowdon speed race and gain speed control over the entire opponent team (all my Pokémon are slow). Goodra Ice Beams Hippowdon (54.9-102.2%), the main threat to Goodra, since it's the piece that must be worn down. This is robust to Gyarados Protecting (likely at 60% HP): Tailwind is still set and Hippowdon is damaged. Next turn with Tailwind, Skarmory (180) and Goodra (160) outspeed Gyarados (146 max) and Hippowdon (99 max), letting me KO Gyarados while Protecting Goodra, then finish Hippowdon with Muddy Water.

Full-HP sun Eruption guarantees Skarmory's death (160-317% — Taunt cannot block a damaging move, Roost+Sturdy don't save it) and KOs 19% Goodra unless it Protects. Hippowdon Protects because Ice Beam, Muddy Water, and Body Press each KO the 33% Hippo before it moves, while HHP->Goodra is redundant in every line where Eruption connects.

Torkoal's sun-boosted Eruption is a guaranteed KO on both Skarmory (167-255%) and Goodra (40-63% on 20% HP), and we cannot KO Torkoal this turn (Muddy Water 24-49%, Body Press 19-33%). Best play: use Goodra's guaranteed Ice Beam KO on Hippowdon (removes the Ground threat that would also hit Aegislash super-effectively) while switching Skarmory to Aegislash to preserve Skarmory and bring in the anti-spread pivot. Aegislash takes only Eruption (91-140%, may survive), and Skarmory stays safe in the back to handle Gyarados-Mega later.

Both active Pokémon fainted; only Skarmory remains usable. Bring Skarmory into slot 1 and pass slot 2 since Tinkaton is also fainted. With one Pokémon left against four, the game is effectively lost, but I'll play it out rather than forfeit while the series is still 1-0.

Skarmory is my only remaining Pokémon and Torkoal's sun-boosted Charcoal Eruption guarantees an OHKO (223-342% of max HP) this turn. With all three other Pokémon fainted, I have no path to win this game. Forfeiting game 2 (series becomes 1-1) preserves a fresh game 3 with my full team rather than wasting resources.

reflections.summary: Won cleanly off the sun core with zero piloting errors. Mega Gyarados's turn-1 Protect baited Tinkaton's Fake Out while Hippowdon's High Horsepower broke its Focus Sash, and Crunch removed it next turn. Swapping Gyarados for Torkoal brought Drought sun for free, and turn 4 Hippowdon's Protect blanked Goodra's Ice Beam while full-HP sun Eruption spread-KO'd Aegislash (super effective) and the HHP-chipped Goodra, isolating a 71% Skarmory with no way back. Team preview was correct — their Steel/Fairy-heavy bring folds to sun — and evolving Gyarados turn 1 was the right Mega call as the Mold Breaker cleaner.
reflections.adjustment: For the decider, lead Torkoal + Hippowdon instead of exposing Gyarados-Mega early: Eruption pressure starts turn 1, Hippowdon's Yawn/Crunch punishes the Aegislash King's Shield opener (protect move turn 1 in both games so far), and Hippowdon bodyblocks Ice Beam — keeping Gyarados fresh and un-Fake-Out-able in the back. Also remove Skarmory before its mid-game Tailwind flips speed against my whole team.

reflections.summary: Lost because the entire team was 2x weak to Fire, and Torkoal's sun-boosted Eruption OHKO'd Aegislash and Goodra, collapsing the board. The team-preview plan was poor: bringing four Fire-weak Pokémon against a known Torkoal with Drought was a critical mistake.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, bring a Fire-resistant or Water/Ground/Rock-type, or preserve Aegislash's Wide Guard to block Eruption. Consider leading with a faster threat to KO Torkoal or using a Pokémon with Storm Drain/Flash Fire to absorb the attack. Also, avoid stacking Fire-weak Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Executing the G3 plan: Torkoal+Hippowdon lead puts full-sun Eruption (2x on Exca, Mawile, Skarmory, Aegi, Tinkaton; KOs Skarmory through Sturdy+Sitrus) turn 1, while Hippo tanks Goodra Ice Beam and punishes Aegi's turn-1 protect habit with Yawn/Crunch. Gyarados-Mega and Ninetales (Encode answer to Aegi protect locks, late-game clean) stay in back; neither lead is the Mega, so Tinkaton's turn-1 Fake Out can't hit it.

Lead Aegislash (Wide Guard shuts down sun-boosted Eruption/Heat Wave/Blizzard/Icy Wind) with Goodra-Hisui (Muddy Water is 2x on Torkoal/Ninetales/Vanilluxe and Thunderbolt is 4x on Gyarados, both special so Intimidate-proof). Back Excadrill for fast Rock Slide/High Horsepower cleanup and Skarmory for Taunt (Hippowdon Yawn, Ninetales Encore) plus Tailwind speed control.

Aegi has opened protect every game (WideGuard blocks Eruption, King's Shield blocks everything aimed at it), so turn-1 value comes from stacking on Tinkaton: Hippo's HHP (never protect-blocked, 2x) breaks Focus Sash, and if Tinkaton Fake Outs Hippo instead, full-power Eruption finishes the 1-HP sash pop; if Aegi ever skips protect, Eruption KOs Shield forme outright. Even when Torkoal eats the Fake Out flinch, it keeps 100% HP for a full-strength turn-2 Eruption against Aegi's reset protect odds.

Torkoal's sun-boosted Charcoal Eruption threatens a guaranteed OHKO on Tinkaton and a likely OHKO on Aegislash, so Wide Guard is mandatory to neutralize the spread. Fake Out on Torkoal adds redundancy (flinches it unless it Protects), fully shutting down the main threat this turn while Hippowdon's single-target hits are survivable (High Horsepower on Aegislash ~44-66%, on Tinkaton saved by Focus Sash). Attacking options are weak (Stone Edge ~31-55%, Play Rough neutral ~18-31%), so the safe defensive play is best.

Eruption + HHP@Aegi: Eruption guarantees the 1% Tinkaton's death in every branch except a successful Wide Guard, while Eruption alone (91-161%) is not a guaranteed Aegi kill — HHP (44-77%, pierces Wide Guard) makes the combined KO guaranteed. Fake Out fails off first-turn, so Torkoal is safe to fire; worst incoming chip (Stone Edge ~44%) can't stop either action.

Aegislash must Wide Guard: Torkoal's sun+Charcoal Eruption can OHKO Aegislash (76-120%) and would KO Tinkaton. Tinkaton at 1 HP must switch out; Skarmory is the safe pivot because it is immune to Hippowdon's High Horsepower (Ground), while Excadrill would risk a 94-139% OHKO from it. Wide Guard blocks Eruption for the whole side, leaving Skarmory at full HP to Taunt Torkoal next turn.

Tool-confirmed: Eruption at current HP is a GUARANTEED OHKO on both Aegislash (91-161.5% vs 50%) and Skarmory (140.7-271.4% through Sturdy+Sitrus), even with the 0.75x spread penalty. Aegi's protect-family counter is at 1/9 after two consecutive Wide Guard successes, so the double-kill lands unless it hits that ~11%. Hippowdon (faster than Torkoal) targets Aegi with High Horsepower as insurance: if Wide Guard somehow succeeds, HHP still does 44.3-77% (~82% KO vs 50%); if King's Shield comes up, Eruption still kills Skarmory. Skarmory Body Press (18.5-26.6%) and Aegi Flash Cannon (23-28%) can't stop Torkoal from firing. Crunch@Skarmory (12-21%) is worthless by comparison.

Aegislash at 51% is threatened by Hippowdon's High Horsepower (44-66% from 51%, likely KO), so King's Shield blocks it. Skarmory Taunts Hippowdon to prevent Yawn — critical because in this format King's Shield does NOT block non-damaging moves, so Yawn would put Aegislash to sleep next turn and lose Wide Guard vs Eruption. Taunting Hippowdon also blocks its Protect and locks it into High Horsepower/Crunch (both blocked by King's Shield or Ground-immune for Skarmory). The remaining risk is Torkoal's Will-O-Wisp (burn is manageable for a support Aegislash) and Eruption breaking Skarmory's Sturdy, which is acceptable since Skarmory outspeeds Torkoal and can still act next turn.

Send Excadrill so it can Mega Evolve and High Horsepower Torkoal before Torkoal acts (Mega Excadrill 110-170 outspeeds Torkoal 36-64). Mega Excadrill's High Horsepower hits Torkoal for ~72-126% (likely KO from 86%; if it doesn't KO, Torkoal is left <=14% and its Eruption is too weak to kill). Mega Excadrill (Def 100) survives Hippowdon's High Horsepower (~56-83%), while base Excadrill is OHKO'd (94-139%). Skarmory is Ground-immune so it survives Hippowdon and walls it with Body Press. Sending Tinkaton instead would sacrifice Skarmory to Eruption and leave a damaged Excadrill in a 1v3; Tinkaton's Stone Edge only chips Torkoal 31-55% and cannot KO it.

Tool-confirmed: Eruption at 87% HP with spread penalty guarantees OHKO on BOTH actives (Excadrill 116.1-220.5%, Skarmory guaranteed from 25%) — only per-target Protect dodges it. Excadrill's fastest counterplay is hitting Torkoal before it moves, but its best HHP caps at 83.2% and cannot KO from 87%, so Eruption always executes; even a max chip leaves Skarmory usually dead and Hippowdon's HHP (61.8-123.2%) cleans Excadrill. If Excadrill instead protects (guaranteed first-use), Skarmory still dies and sun persists one more turn for a repeat Eruption vs 1/3 protect odds. Taunt locks Hippowdon out of Yawn/Protect, so HHP@Excadrill is strictly its best action.

Gyarados replaces Torkoal: entry Intimidate weakens both attackers, it is immune to Excadrill's High Horsepower and resists Iron Head, and Mega Evolving now adds a 155-Atk cleaner. Excadrill always outspeeds even Mega Gyarados (135–170 vs 133), but its only good hit back is Rock Slide (~57-79.6% at neutral Attack, roughly halved by Intimidate, never an OHKO from full). Ninetales' Heat Wave double-KO line fails to fresh Protects from both foes (neither has used Protect this game) plus 90% accuracy, so Gyarados is strictly safer. Hippowdon is Taunted and passes.

Mega Excadrill High Horsepower (68-120%) + Skarmory Body Press (19-33%) guarantees Torkoal KO from 86% (min combined ~87%), stopping the sun-boosted Eruption that OHKOs both actives. Mega raises Def to 120 so Hippowdon's High Horsepower (~63-93%) is survivable, and Piercing Drill chips through Protect if Torkoal protects; Skarmory survives Hippowdon's Crunch at 26%.

Hippo HHP guarantees Exca-Mega's removal (47-82.2% vs 21%, 95% acc); Mega Gyara always outspeeds Skarmory and Crunch (Dark STAB post-Mega) nearly guarantees the KO on 25% before it can Roost/Tailwind, while Waterfall is resisted.

Excadrill-Mega is my only real damage source and both Gyarados Waterfall (28.9-41.7%, guaranteed KO from 22%) and Hippowdon High Horsepower (62-94.1%, guaranteed KO) KO it this turn, so Protect is mandatory to keep it alive and waste the opponent's likely double-target. Skarmory survives any current attack (Crunch 12.8-18%, Waterfall weaker in sun, High Horsepower immune), so it sets Tailwind: it flips Skarmory's speed vs Gyarados (90->180 vs 111-146), insures against a Gyarados Dragon Dance outspeeding Excadrill next turn, and sets up future Rock Slide flinch attempts. My damage is crippled (-1 Atk, spread penalty: Rock Slide only 22.8-43.5% vs Gyarados), so preserving Excadrill and Tinkaton's Fake Out sack is the only path to a comeback.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double attack on separate targets wins the endgame: Waterfall is tool-confirmed to guarantee the KO on Excadrill-Mega (23-42% even while sun-halved vs 21%, and sun is gone), and Hippowdon's High Horsepower (2x) trivially kills Tinkaton at 1% with Sash consumed. Crucially, Tinkaton's re-entry makes Fake Out live this turn — it can flinch only ONE attacker, so splitting targets guarantees at least one KO regardless; if both land, the game ends immediately. Neither of my mons can be KO'd from full this turn (Exca is -1 Atk, HHP ~18-25% into Mega Gyarados; Play Rough ~60-72% but non-lethal), and every miss/fail branch leaves a trivially cleanable 1% Tinkaton or 21% Excadrill facing a guaranteed kill next turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Both my Pokémon are at death's door (Excadrill 22%, Tinkaton 1%) while the foe has two full-HP threats plus an unrevealed 4th. I cannot KO Hippowdon (combined max ~64%), so the only meaningful play is to concentrate fire on Gyarados-Mega: Excadrill High Horsepower (24-42%) + Tinkaton Play Rough (44-77%) gives a real chance to remove the biggest threat if both hit and Tinkaton outspeeds. This maximizes whatever small win probability remains.

Excadrill-Mega is the foe's last Pokémon at 21%. Both attacks independently guarantee the KO (Heat Wave 83.9-156.8%, High Horsepower 47-82.2%), so doubling gives near-certain victory even against its unknown Piercing Drill ability, a possible speed win, or a lucky Protect. Even if it outspeeds and OHKOs Ninetales (90.9-126% range), Hippowdon's attack still ends the game.

Excadrill-Mega is my only remaining Pokémon at 22% HP against two full-health foes. High Horsepower can at best KO Ninetales (67.8-131.1%, not guaranteed), but Hippowdon survives and its super-effective High Horsepower will KO Excadrill, leaving me with no Pokémon. Rock Slide cannot KO either (Ninetales 26.7-52.7%, Hippowdon 3.7-6.6%). There is no line that wins this game, so I concede.

reflections.summary: Game 3 and the series (2-1) were won by executing the prepared sun-trade script almost flawlessly with zero decision errors. Preview plan was correct: the double-Drought + Hippowdon + Mega Gyarados four matched a steel-heavy Wide Guard team, and Mega went on Gyarados, the only mon they had no Water answer for. Execution: Hippowdon's High Horsepower broke Tinkaton's Sash on turn 1 and removed Aegislash before King's Shield stalling mattered, while forced Wide Guards blanked Eruption but bought nothing; Torkoal's planned early trade to Excadrill-Mega/Body Press triggered the Intimidate pivot into Mega Gyarados, which removed Taunt-locked Skarmory and soaked the board while Hippowdon eliminated Tinkaton. When Tinkaton's Play Rough took Gyarados exactly inside the calibrated 60-72% window, the between-game Ninetales insurance proved its worth: her Drought refresh plus a full Hippowdon stranded a lone 21%, -1 Atk Excadrill with no win condition. The adjustments helped, nothing backfired.
reflections.adjustment: Recalibrate two numbers before a rematch: Excadrill-Mega's High Horsepower did ~35% to Mega Gyarados even at -1 Atk (well above the old 18-25% log), so Mega Gyarados cannot afford to take two of them — pivot or Protect sooner; and Hippowdon's High Horsepower rolled ~79% into Excadrill-Mega (top of the 47-82% band, never an OHKO). Versus their confirmed Tinkaton/Aegislash lead with Wide Guard spam, consider opening single-target (High Horsepower) instead of Eruption, or baiting Wide Guard with Protect, since their guard turns accomplished nothing. Verify whether Ninetales (167) outruns Jolly Excadrill-Mega — never tested. Scout for Mawile-Mega and Goodra-Hisui, benched in both decisive games and likely to debut next time. Keep avoiding Protect reliance against Excadrill until its 'Piercing Drill' ability is identified.

reflections.summary: The series was lost 1-2 because the team-preview plan and in-game execution both hinged on a single roll that failed: Excadrill-Mega's High Horsepower was supposed to KO Torkoal from 86% but only brought it to 3%, leaving Skarmory to waste a turn finishing it off. This allowed Hippowdon to freely pressure Aegislash, who went down to repeated High Horsepowers, and gave Gyarados-Mega a clean entry to clean up. The four brought (Excadrill-Mega, Aegislash, Tinkaton, Skarmory) were too Ground-weak and lacked a reliable answer to Hippowdon, who walled the team and chipped away. The decision to bring Excadrill-Mega over Mawile-Mega was reasonable on paper (Ground coverage for Torkoal), but the team had no way to punish Hippowdon's free turns, and Gyarados-Mega's Intimidate + Mold Breaker combination dismantled the physical attackers. The series was ultimately lost at team preview: the roster lacked a special attacker or a way to pressure Hippowdon, and the opponent's weather core (Torkoal + Ninetales) plus Gyarados-Mgo was too much for the one-note physical offense to break through.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a future series, I would bring a different four: specifically, I would strongly consider Gholdengo (left behind) over Tinkaton or Aegislash, as it provides a special Ghost/Steel presence that resists Ground and can threaten Hippowdon with STAB Make It Rain or Shadow Ball. I would also consider Metagross (left behind) as a Bullet Punch user to pick off weakened Torkoal and Gyarados, or as a Trick Room answer. The core issue was that Excadrill-Mega was the only real damage dealer, and once Intimidate or a Ground move came in, the team crumbled. I would also lead differently: instead of leading Aegislash + Tinkaton, I would lead Excadrill-Mega + Skarmory to threaten immediate pressure on Torkoal and pivot into a better position. The plan to KO Torkoal turn 1 was correct, but I should have had a backup plan (e.g., a priority move or a faster pivot) in case it survived at 1%. Finally, I would have saved Tinkaton's Focus Sash better—using it as a sack was fine, but I should have kept it out of range of Hippowdon's High Horsepower to preserve a revenge killer for Gyarados.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard + Sableye for Fake Out into Mega Charizard Y sun offense; bring Empoleon as the Mega Gardevoir wall and Dragapult for Hydreigon/Kingambit speed control and Sash trade.

Lead Mega Lucario and Choice Scarf Hydreigon to pressure Dragapult, Empoleon, and Slurpuff immediately; preserve Greninja as Focus Sash insurance against Garchomp and Charizard, with Volcarona providing redirection, special-attack control, and Tailwind.

Mega evolve Charizard Y to set sun and survive Hydreigon's Draco, then use sun-boosted Heat Wave to KO/threaten Lucario. Sableye's Fake Out flinches Hydreigon, which cannot Protect due to Choice Scarf, preventing the biggest turn-1 KO threat to Charizard.
Mega Lucario Protects against Fake Out, burn, and sun-boosted Heat Wave while gaining Speed for next turn; Hydreigon pressures Charizard immediately with the strongest available attack.

Charizard's sun-boosted Heat Wave is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Lucario and also leaves Hydreigon at roughly 15-33%. Sableye's Prankster Quash on Lucario goes first against non-priority moves, forcing any fast Mega Lucario attack to move last so Charizard removes it before it can land Close Combat/Meteor Mash; its status moves would fail into Hydreigon because of Prankster vs Dark.
Preserve Mega Lucario from a guaranteed sun-boosted Heat Wave KO by switching to Volcarona, while Scarf Hydreigon pressures Charizard with Draco Meteor and survives Heat Wave.

Hydreigon's Choice Scarf Draco Meteor guarantees the KO on 21% Charizard before it can move, so Charizard pivots to Empoleon, which resists Dragon and can OHKO Hydreigon next turn with Ice Beam. Sableye stays and uses Prankster Taunt on Volcarona to stop Rage Powder, Tailwind, and Protect from disrupting the incoming Ice Beam.
Rage Powder redirects Sableye's priority disruption and Charizard's single-target attacks, allowing Hydreigon to move first naturally and secure the guaranteed KO on Charizard if Draco Meteor hits.

Empoleon's Ice Beam is a guaranteed KO on the 21% Hydreigon, removing the Choice-locked attacker. Sableye's Prankster Quash makes the Taunted Volcarona move last, so its only available move (Struggle Bug) cannot lower Empoleon before Ice Beam or otherwise disrupt the KO.

Double switch preserves both weakened Pokémon. Lucario safely takes the likely Ice Beam aimed at Hydreigon and immediately pressures Empoleon, while Greninja is relatively unbothered by a likely Will-O-Wisp into Volcarona's slot.

Empoleon Protecting avoids Mega Lucario's guaranteed-OHKO Close Combat, while Sableye's Prankster Will-O-Wisp burns Lucario (a non-Dark target), halving its physical threat and preserving Empoleon for the next turn.
Protect blocks Sableye's likely priority Will-O-Wisp into Lucario while Greninja safely pressures Sableye; Empoleon's attacks are low-impact into this board.

Pivot Empoleon out into Dragapult to dodge Lucario's guaranteed Close Combat KO and preserve Empoleon; Sableye's Prankster Will-O-Wisp targets Lucario-Mega to burn its physical pressure before it moves (Protect chance discounted).
Preserve Lucario from priority Will-O-Wisp by switching to Volcarona while Greninja pressures the weakened Sableye with Dark Pulse.

Sableye at 1 HP would likely be picked off by Greninja's Water Shuriken before it can act, so pivot it into Empoleon, which takes Greninja's hits well. Dragapult uses Draco Meteor on Volcarona to try to KO it before Tailwind goes up.
Dark Pulse pressures Dragapult while Struggle Bug guarantees Sableye’s KO, chips Dragapult through Focus Sash, and lowers its Special Attack if Volcarona acts.
Bring in Mega Lucario to threaten Dragapult with Bullet Punch and Empoleon with Close Combat, preserving Hydreigon for later cleanup.

Empoleon Protects to dodge Lucario-Mega's guaranteed Close Combat OHKO. Dragapult stays in and Will-O-Wisps Lucario-Mega; if Greninja uses Water Shuriken Dragapult faints before moving, but any non-priority line lands a key burn against the main physical threat.

Switch Sableye to preserve Charizard as the win condition. Sableye is already at 1 HP but can use Fake Out at +3 priority on its first turn in, letting it disrupt an opponent before Water Shuriken or Bullet Punch.
Water Shuriken guarantees the priority KO on Dragapult, while Close Combat guarantees an OHKO on Empoleon if it does not Protect or switch.

Sableye's Fake Out is fastest and locks down Mega Lucario so it cannot Close Combat Empoleon. Empoleon Flash Cannons Greninja to chip it out of full-HP Focus Sash range, setting up Charizard's sun Solar Beam/Heat Wave cleanly next turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Water Shuriken has priority and guarantees the KO on Sableye before its Prankster status moves, while Close Combat guarantees the OHKO on Empoleon if it does not Protect.

Charizard wins only if it survives the likely double priority from Greninja and Mega Lucario, so protect it. Empoleon fishes for a freeze on Greninja with Ice Beam to create an opening for Charizard next turn.
Greninja outspeeds and guarantees the KO on Charizard with Dark Pulse, while Lucario guarantees the OHKO on Empoleon with Close Combat.

Only Charizard remains and both opponent priority attacks move first; combined minimum damage from Greninja Water Shuriken plus Lucario Bullet Punch exceeds Charizard's remaining HP, so Charizard cannot reliably act, and no move can win the 1v2. Concede game 1.
Greninja outspeeds and Dark Pulse guarantees the KO; Lucario Protects against any attack if Charizard survives via Protect.

reflections.summary: Team preview lost the game: Mega Charizard Y was a reasonable bring into Mega Lucario/Volcarona, but base Sableye was blanked by Hydreigon and Greninja because Prankster Quash/Will-o-Wisp fail on Dark-types, and Volcarona is Fire-immune. That left no reliable speed control or disruption, so Scarf Hydreigon Draco Meteor’d Charizard to 21% on turn 2 and the team never reclaimed tempo. Piloting had no flagged errors, but Sableye was dead weight outside Fake Out and one Taunt.
reflections.adjustment: Bench Sableye against this Hydreigon/Greninja double-Dark build and bring Garchomp or Slurpuff instead; if you bring Slurpuff, set Sticky Web to fix the speed matchup, and Protect or switch Charizard around Hydreigon’s Draco Meteor.

reflections.summary: Won because Choice Scarf Hydreigon immediately reduced Mega Charizard Y to 20%, then Greninja’s Dark Pulse and priority removed Sableye and Focus Sash Dragapult while Mega Lucario broke Empoleon. Team preview was well matched: Hydreigon/Lucario/Greninja/Volcarona covered all four opposing picks, and evolving Lucario rather than using Mega Gardevoir was correct. Piloting was clean, preserving the needed attackers through Sableye’s disruption and Empoleon’s Protects.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same four and Mega Lucario if this composition returns, but anticipate adaptation by targeting Sableye early with Greninja while preserving Volcarona for redirection or Tailwind; this limits Fake Out, Taunt, Quash, and Will-O-Wisp before Lucario attacks Empoleon.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard + Slurpuff: immediate Mega-Y sun/Heat Wave pressure plus Fairy spread for Scarf Hydreigon, with Sticky Web available to slow grounded Greninja/Lucario/Volcarona. Garchomp and Dragapult in back cover Steel/Volcarona and Hydra/Greninja respectively.

Lead Choice Scarf Hydreigon with Volcarona to pressure Charizard immediately while Rage Powder absorbs Fake Out; Hydreigon also ignores Prankster Quash. Preserve Mega Lucario for Empoleon and Greninja for Sableye and Dragapult cleanup.

Mega Evolve Charizard before moves so Drought is active and Charizard-Y's higher Special Defense lets it survive Hydreigon's Draco; Heat Wave and Dazzling Gleam are both spread, bypassing Rage Powder and giving the best chance to remove Hydreigon while chipping Volcarona.

Draco Meteor pressures an immediate Charizard KO, while Struggle Bug weakens both special attackers before Slurpuff acts and usually before Charizard, improving survival if Charizard endures or Protects.
Bring Lucario to threaten Charizard with Bullet Punch and Slurpuff with Meteor Mash while Volcarona can provide Rage Powder support.
Switch Charizard out to Dragapult so Mega Lucario's Bullet Punch cannot pick off the 15% Charizard, while Slurpuff Dazzling Gleam chips Lucario into Dragapult sun-boosted Fire Blast range next turn.
Protect Mega Lucario from the guaranteed sun-boosted Heat Wave OHKO while Volcarona establishes Tailwind before likely fainting, enabling Greninja and Mega Lucario to pressure both foes next turn.

Dragapult's sun-boosted Fire Blast into Mega Lucario is our best pressure: if Volcarona Rage Powders, it still KOes Volcarona; if not, it likely removes or heavily damages Lucario. Protect keeps Slurpuff safe from Lucario's Meteor Mash while Dragapult takes the offense.
Meteor Mash guarantees the Slurpuff KO if it hits, while Rage Powder redirects Dragapult’s otherwise lethal Fire Blast away from Lucario, preserving Mega Lucario under Tailwind.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Slurpuff Helping Hand at +5 resolves before Lucario can KO it, and boosted sun Fire Blast from Dragapult is a guaranteed OHKO onto Mega Lucario. This removes their main threat while Focus Sash keeps Dragapult safe from a single hit if they split attacks.

Do not forfeit. Bring full-health Garchomp as the switch-in: Yache Berry lets it survive Greninja's Ice Beam, and Brick Break is super effective into Greninja. Charizard-Mega-Y is too low at 15% and would be outsped and KOed before contributing reliably under Tailwind.
Meteor Mash guarantees Slurpuff's KO if it does not Protect, while Dark Pulse maximizes damage into Dragapult and can reduce it to Focus Sash before it moves under Tailwind.

Double-target Greninja. Garchomp's Brick Break is its strongest reliable hit into Greninja, and Dragapult's Draco Meteor softens Greninja first (Dragapult is faster than Garchomp after Greninja acts) so Garchomp can finish through Focus Sash. Even if Greninja removes 1 HP Dragapult first, Garchomp still gets a strong Brick Break and we retain a favorable finish path.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Use the final Tailwind turn to guarantee the KO on Dragapult before it can attack; Dark Pulse is accurate and comfortably removes it from 1%.

reflections.summary: Game 3 and the series were won because Charizard-Mega-Y was the correct Mega pick and its sun-boosted spread damage broke the opposing core once Tailwind was stalled out. The between-game adjustment to preserve Slurpuff as the Hydreigon answer and use double Protect on the final Tailwind turn worked cleanly. Slurpuff's Dazzling Gleam removed the Choice-locked Hydreigon, and Charizard cleaned Volcarona. The four brought suited the matchup; Dragapult and Garchomp were expendable but acceptable pivots/sacks, and no adjustment backfired.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Charizard-Y + Slurpuff core and the double-Protect Tailwind stall for a future series. Do not rely on Heat Wave to OHKO Volcarona; use Air Slash or a second spread hit to finish it. The registered six were adequate, though Garchomp and Dragapult were the weakest links here; a sturdier pivot could be considered if the sets support it.

reflections.summary: Game 3 was lost because the composition could not finish Mega Charizard Y while also containing Slurpuff. Tailwind and Mega Lucario initially helped: Lucario removed Garchomp, while Choice Scarf Hydreigon eliminated Dragapult and reduced Charizard to closing range. However, Protect cycles consumed Tailwind, early spread damage depleted Volcarona and Greninja, and Hydreigon became locked into Dark Pulse with Slurpuff still available to KO it with Dazzling Gleam. The Mega Lucario plus Volcarona adjustment therefore partly worked but ultimately backfired structurally: Volcarona provided speed control yet too little closing pressure, while the planned early Slurpuff removal and Greninja preservation never materialized. With zero recorded decision errors, this was primarily a team-preview and matchup-plan loss rather than a piloting failure. Mega Lucario was a suitable Mega choice and the four had a coherent plan, but Hydreigon and Greninja overlapped in attacking Dragapult while leaving the Charizard-Slurpuff endgame poorly covered. Preparation was serviceable against Dragapult and Garchomp but lacked a reliable combined answer to Charizard's spread pressure, Slurpuff's protection/support, and repeated Protect turns. Nothing revealed about the unregistered Mega options establishes a materially better alternative for this opponent.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Mega Lucario as the preferred Mega, but do not center the game plan on passive Volcarona Tailwind support. Bring a four that can apply sustained simultaneous pressure to Charizard and Slurpuff, and treat removing Slurpuff as essential before committing Hydreigon to Dark Pulse. Preserve Greninja's Focus Sash for meaningful Charizard or Garchomp pressure instead of using it primarily to finish Dragapult; retain Lucario's priority as the cleaner for Dragapult's Sash. Within the registered six, test whether Kingambit or Mega Gardevoir can replace one of the overlapping Dark attackers or the low-damage support slot, but their supplied information is insufficient to claim either was definitively better. For future registration, prioritize a non-Mega slot that remains threatening into both Charizard and Slurpuff rather than replacing Lucario with one of the left-behind Mega-only alternatives.
